research:strategy-evidence.summary:
Method note: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this sweep began, and every academic/quant host tried via WebFetch (arXiv, SSRN mirrors, NBER, BIS, MDPI, Springer, Wiley, T&F, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, dblp, Wayback, Quantpedia, Robot Wealth, Alpha Architect, Wikipedia) was blocked by the egress proxy. The sweep therefore ran ~20 GitHub code/repo searches (GitHub MCP) plus raw.githubusercontent.com fetches, which surfaced (a) full-text markdown conversions of three primary papers (Gerritsen et al. 2020 FRL; Hudson & Urquhart 2021 Ann. Oper. Res.; a 2025 Financial Innovation triple-barrier paper), (b) a detailed 2026-09-17 five-part literature review on crypto strategy cost tolerance, and (c) several 2026 practitioner research logs that tested the exact strategy families asked about. Claims from secondhand extractions are marked medium confidence with the primary DOI/arXiv given in the text.

Bottom line for the user's $5-10k "flip for 2-3%" pool: the peer-reviewed and 2026-preprint evidence is consistently negative for short-horizon spot BTC trading once realistic fees are charged. (1) Intraday mean reversion: a persistent 15-minute reversal exists in BTC/crypto (Kitron & Wengrowicz, arXiv 2608.21888, Aug 2026) but its gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp/trade versus >=5 bp cheapest round-trip; Jaquart et al. 2021 found 1-60 min ML predictability only <=15 min and unprofitable after costs; RSI and Bollinger-band rules on daily BTC significantly UNDERPERFORM buy-and-hold (Gerritsen 2020, p<0.01), and Resta 2020 found buy-and-hold beats every TA rule at 5-min resolution while only daily SMAs help. (2) Hourly ML/momentum: Bysik & Slepaczuk (arXiv 2606.00060, May 2026) show gross Sharpe 1.27-2.59 flips to -1.16 to -1.82 at just 10 bps all-in cost; a cost-aware filter that cuts trades 10,619->251 restores +65% ARC/Sharpe 1.09 but with no statistically significant outperformance vs buy-and-hold after Holm correction. (3) Break-even costs: Hudson & Urquhart's ~15,000-rule study puts BTC break-even one-way costs at 57-66 bp (to 2017) and finds NO out-of-sample BTC predictability in H1 2018; Coinbase Advanced entry-tier fees are reportedly 0.50% maker/0.90% taker as of 2026-09-16 (previously 0.60/1.20), i.e. a 1.0-1.8% round trip that alone consumes most of a 2-3% target. (4) Grid trading: a static grid's expected return is analytically ~zero before fees and negative after (Chen, Chen & Jang, arXiv 2506.11921); it is a short-volatility bet that loses in trends. (5) Fixed take-profit exits: under a martingale the bracket cannot change expectancy (optional stopping); under positive drift a take-profit is a cost (Acar & Toffel), and a 2020-2025 BTC backtest with 0.1% fees found every sell rule (25% profit target, Bollinger-middle, EMA exits) cut CAGR from 71% to 13-23%. (6) Funding/basis: BTC carry Sharpe fell from 6.45 (2020-25) to 4.06 (2024) to negative in 2025; practitioner 2026 tests of funding-extreme fades found every forward-return CI includes zero; no peer-reviewed paper shows funding rate predicts returns out of sample. (7) Time-of-day/weekend: day-of-week effects replicate for BTC in daily data but vanish under hourly disaggregation (a Sunday 23:00 UTC price-discovery artifact); no weekend-vs-weekday return gap 2016-2024; a 2026 multi-test harness KILLed day-of-week. (8) What does have support: slow daily/weekly trend filters. Price/MA ratios (5-100 day) raised BTC Sharpe from 1.9 to 2.1-2.5 and cut max drawdown from 89.5% to 64-70% (Detzel et al. 2021, 2010-2018; break-even one-way fee 1.1-4.0%), slow 12-week signals beat fast ones in BTC (Kang & Ryu 2026), a Donchian-ensemble with vol sizing reports Sharpe ~1.58 net of 0.1-0.5% fees (Zarattini 2025, secondhand), and a 50/200 golden-cross 2020-2025 test gave 44% CAGR/-57% DD vs HODL 63%/-77%: trend filters mainly buy drawdown reduction, not extra return, and per-market crypto trend Sharpe is "positive but small" (Man Group). Implication for the paper-trading design: compare 1.5%/2%/3-5% take-profit variants against buy-and-hold and against a 200-day/12-week trend filter under the user's actual fee tier, log the number of trials to deflate Sharpe, and expect that the only variants likely to survive are low-turnover ones.

claims.claim: Bysik & Slepaczuk (Univ. of Warsaw, arXiv 2606.00060, May 2026), ~70,000 hourly BTC-USDT bars 2018-2026 in a 27-fold walk-forward: naive sign-based ML strategies earned +73.5% (XGBoost, Sharpe 1.27), +72.4% (LSTM, 1.45) and +129% (iTransformer, 2.59) at zero cost but -64.0%/-50.7%/-83.9% (Sharpe -1.25/-1.16/-1.82) once a 10 bp all-in cost per unit turnover was charged; a cost-aware execution filter cutting trades from 10,619 to 251 restored long-only XGBoost to +65.4% ARC / Sharpe 1.09, yet bootstrap/Holm-adjusted tests show no statistically significant Sharpe outperformance versus buy-and-hold. Read via secondhand extractions in GitHub research logs (Vito-bc/crypto-orchestra 01-execution-cost-structure.md; HCH725/alpha-strategy-research; sshirazshahid scout note), not the arXiv page.

Kitron & Wengrowicz, 'Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement' (arXiv 2608.21888, 22 Aug 2026): 183 Binance USDT spot pairs vs 187 US equities, Jan 2025-Feb 2026 plus a frozen 6-month holdout to Aug 2026. A persistent 15-minute reversal exists in ~90% of crypto pairs (AUC 0.531 vs 0.499 for equities) and decays to no-skill within hours, but 'the gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp per trade' against a 5 bp cheapest round-trip and 10-20 bp taker costs: 'not exploitable under benchmark spot-cost assumptions'. Replication code: github.com/nadav2/short-horizon-reversion (README fetched). Secondhand via Vito-bc review and nofx-papers abstract file.

Hudson & Urquhart, 'Technical trading and cryptocurrencies', Annals of Operations Research 297 (2021) (full text read from a markdown conversion hosted at github.com/fisaarpelesjo/nautilus): 14,919 rules across five families on daily BTC/ETH/XRP/LTC to end-2017. Break-even one-way transaction costs for Bitcoin top out at 66.41 bp (CoinDesk series) and 57.51 bp (Bitstamp), range 7.88-147.56 bp across all coins/rules; the paper notes prevailing BTC costs were ~50 bp. Rules mainly reduce drawdown severity vs buy-and-hold. In the pure out-of-sample H1 2018 (bear) test the best in-sample rules gave NEGATIVE annualized return and Sharpe for both BTC series while staying positive for LTC/XRP/ETH ('there is no predictability for Bitcoin in the out-of-sample period').

Gerritsen, Bouri, Ramezanifar & Roubaud, 'The profitability of technical trading rules in the Bitcoin market', Finance Research Letters 34:101263 (2020), daily BTC Feb 2011-Jan 2019, Ledoit-Wolf bootstrapped Sharpe tests (full text read via markdown mirror at github.com/fisaarpelesjo/nautilus): the countertrend rules RSI and Bollinger bands 'significantly underperform the buy-and-hold benchmark, but in some instances even yield negative Sharpe ratios' (Bollinger diff vs B&H -11.55/-5.34/-3.43 bp daily Sharpe, p<=0.02 across three strategies); only trading-range breakout consistently beat buy-and-hold (150-200 day lookbacks best), with outperformance concentrated in strongly trending sub-periods (2013-14, 2017-18) and underperformance in the quiet 2015-2016 period. The authors explicitly leave transaction costs to future research.

Resta, Pagnottoni & De Giuli, 'Technical Analysis on the Bitcoin Market: Trading Opportunities or Investors' Pitfall?', Risks 8(2):44 (2020), BTC at both 5-minute and daily resolution Jan 2012-Aug 2019: 'trading on daily data is more profitable than going intraday... the Buy and Hold strategy outperforms the examined alternatives on an intraday basis, while Simple Moving Averages yield the best performances when dealing with daily data.' Quoted in a GitHub knowledge-base extraction (CodeGateSoftware/keel source-74); primary not accessed.

Grid trading: Chen, Chen & Jang, 'Dynamic Grid Trading Strategy: From Zero Expectation to Market Outperformance' (arXiv 2506.11921, 2025) derive analytically that under a symmetric random walk with liquidation at the lower bound a static grid's expected return is essentially zero before fees and therefore net-negative after fees; their enhanced dynamic variant beats BTC/ETH buy-and-hold on 1-minute data Jan 2021-Jul 2024 mainly by retaining directional beta, and its cost assumptions are not stated in the abstract. Two independent 2026 GitHub critiques (CarlDog/wobblebot external validation, Silent47boryara/searching-for-edge 'grid-bot illusion') conclude a grid is a short-volatility bet that loses in trends and that grid spacing must clear roughly 2x the round-trip fee to profit; no direct peer-reviewed crypto-grid drawdown study was found.

Fixed take-profit exits: the 2026-09-17 literature review (Vito-bc/crypto-orchestra, 04-momentum-breakout-evidence.md) documents that under a martingale a stop/target bracket cannot change expectancy (optional stopping theorem) and only redistributes probability between hit rate and payoff size; under positive drift a take-profit is a cost. Acar & Toffel ('Stop-loss and Investment Returns', Institute of Actuaries 2000) found targets underperform their own theoretical expectation (S&P 500 take-profit at 1.10%: realised 6.30% annualised vs 8.95% expected) and called take-profits 'counter-productive since they are not triggered often enough and do not prevent very large losses'. Kaminski & Lo's positive stop-loss result is for monthly futures over 55 years, not intraday crypto.

Open-source BTC backtest (yongkangc/btc-trading-strategy-analysis, Yahoo daily data Jan 2020-Oct 2025, 0.1% fee on every trade): buy-and-hold/buy-the-dip without sell rules returned 1,576-2,100% (CAGR 63-71%, Sharpe 1.11-1.21, max DD -76.6%), whereas every sell rule tested cut CAGR to 13-23%: 25% profit target 21.2% CAGR/Sharpe 0.71/DD -64.6% (77 trades), Bollinger-middle exit 22.4%/0.86/-48.7% (740 trades), 50-day SMA exit 13.1%/0.52/-60%; a 50/200 golden-cross timing strategy gave 44.3% CAGR, Sharpe 1.03, DD -56.6% (11 trades). Author's conclusion: buy-and-hold beat active sell rules during the bull period even after optimizing exits; excessive trading (900-1,200 trades) produced severe fee drag. Single practitioner backtest, bull-regime sample.

Fee floor: per the 2026-09-17 review (Vito-bc/crypto-orchestra 01-execution-cost-structure.md), multiple outlets reported that Coinbase changed its Advanced spot fee schedule on 2026-09-16 to an entry-level 0.50% maker / 0.90% taker (down from 0.60% / 1.20%), with the first volume-tier threshold cut from $25,000 to $10,000; the repository's own API probe on 2026-09-17 read pricing_tier 'Intro', maker 0.005, taker 0.009 (single reading). The review states the literature's cost assumptions cluster at 4-60 bp and that no peer-reviewed study tests a >=1.5% round-trip cost on spot; a 1.0-1.8% round trip at retail Coinbase tiers exceeds every BTC break-even cost Hudson & Urquhart report. Coinbase's own page was not reachable to confirm.

Funding-rate/basis signals: Borri, Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu ('Cryptocurrency as an Investable Asset Class', arXiv 2510.14435, 2025) report BTC cash-and-carry Sharpe 6.45 over Aug 2020-May 2025 (mean funding ~8%/yr, vol 0.8%) falling to 4.06 from 2024 and turning negative in 2025 as spot ETFs and delta-neutral products compressed the premium; a Dec 2025-Feb 2026 practitioner replication (dolgoonnn/rl-trading-agent) found structural carry of ~7-8%/yr net but 'threshold-gated harvesting is uniformly net-negative' and a negative-control composite of funding signals had net Sharpe -2.9 (SSRN 6701738, 2022-2026). Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov 'Crypto Carry' (BIS WP 1087) frame carry as limits-to-arbitrage compensation whose high values predict crashes, not a return forecast.

Funding-extreme fade as a directional signal: a 2026-08 practitioner harness (Cyh1368/agentic-quant-desk H2-funding-extremes) using Binance and Hyperliquid funding 2020-2026 found BTC +12h forward return after extreme funding of +42 bp with 95% CI [-28, +114] and 'every fwd-return CI includes 0 and overlaps its null band'; the same fade rule flipped from +37.6% to -81.3% depending on which venue's funding series was used, so the effect was classified as noise. A separate thesis literature note (anilmercanoglu-debug/projectA research.md) states 'there is no rigorous peer-reviewed paper showing funding rate predicts future returns out-of-sample' and that the extreme-funding-reversal claim is grey literature. A 2026-09-15 basis-crowding overlay on a vol-targeted BTC/ETH book scored a FAIL (Sharpe diff 0.001 vs benchmark, p=0.57; forward-30d BTC return after 'crowded' days +9.2% vs +5.4% otherwise, i.e. the BIS crash-after-high-carry pattern did not reproduce at that horizon).

Day-of-week/weekend effects: a Financial Innovation (2023) study (10.1186/s40854-023-00499-x) finds day-of-week effects replicate for BTC but not ETH or ADA, and weekend-vs-weekday return gaps are absent in the full sample and every subsample (2016-2019, 2020-2023, early 2024) despite lower weekend volatility; an ML-Quants 2024 hourly re-examination finds the daily 'Monday effect' collapses into a single Sunday 23:00-00:00 UTC window and all weekly-seasonal significance vanishes once intraday fixed effects are controlled (an aggregation/bar-boundary artifact), with the BTC Monday effect decaying to nothing post-2015. Secondhand via Vito-bc 04-momentum-breakout-evidence.md and Orrimp/-Vibe-Trading papers.md.

Trend/regime filters on BTC: Detzel, Liu, Strauss, Zhou & Zhu, 'Learning and predictability via technical analysis: Evidence from bitcoin...' (Financial Management 50(1), 2021; SSRN 3115846), BTC daily Oct 2010-Jan 2018: price-to-moving-average ratios (5-100 day; 200-day NOT tested) predict returns in- and out-of-sample; MA timing (long above MA, else T-bills) raised Sharpe from 1.9 (buy-and-hold) to 2.1-2.5 and cut max drawdown from 89.5% to 64.3-70.3% (second-half sample DD 73.4% -> 33.5%); outperformance 'largely stems from the MA strategy having less severe and much shorter drawdowns'. One-way fee that would eliminate the alpha: MA50 2.74%, MA100 3.96% (turnover 5.0%/2.7% per day), but break-evens are inflated by 2010-2018 gross alpha (BTC excess return 213.6%/yr). Secondhand via Vito-bc 02/03 review files.

Kang & Ryu (Risk Management, 2026, 10.1057/s41283-026-00234-7): across BTC time-series-momentum signal speeds, slow 12-week-baseline signals beat intermediate and fast ones (the inverse of the equity pattern), with speed acting as risk management; no cost figures visible. The 2026-09-17 review concludes slow multi-week trend is 'the only signal speed where documented edge direction and cost tolerance coincide', since daily-bar MA50/MA100 rules turn over ~2.7-5%/day (a full round trip every 20-40 days) and would incur ~9-16%/yr drag at a 0.9% one-way cost.

Zarattini, Pagani & Barbon, 'Catching Crypto Trends: A Tactical Approach for Bitcoin and Altcoins' (SSRN 5209907, Apr 2025; Swiss Finance Institute WP 25-80): ensemble of Donchian-channel breakout models with volatility-based sizing on a rotational top-20 liquid-coin universe, survivorship-free since Jan 2015-Mar 2025, reports CAGR ~30%, Sharpe 1.58, Sortino 2.03, alpha +10.8-14% vs BTC, net of fees tested at 0.10-0.50%. Figures are secondhand (Concretum summary) and the reviewer could not open the SSRN PDF; the highest fee tested (0.50%) is well below retail Coinbase round-trip costs, and it is a 20-asset vol-targeted portfolio, not a single-asset result.

Man Group, 'In Crypto We Trend': for institutional crypto trend-following 'the Sharpe ratio of an individual market is positive but small'; portfolio Sharpe peaks at 10-15 coins for crossover models and ~10 for breakout models, beyond which transaction costs and slippage outweigh diversification; the authors note their Sharpes are 'higher than expected... probably a function of the short history'. Implication: single-asset BTC trend edge is small; the edge is a diversification effect. Secondhand via Vito-bc 04 review.

Quantpedia, 'Revisiting Trend-following and Mean-reversion Strategies in Bitcoin' (12 Sep 2024): original study Nov 2015-Feb 2022; genuine out-of-sample window 4 Feb 2022-20 Aug 2024 covering a full bear leg. The trend-following (MAX) rule 'remains alive and well' out-of-sample while the mean-reversion (MIN) rule delivered 'low or even negative returns'. Weakness: no CAGR, Sharpe or drawdown figures reported (charts and prose only). Secondhand via Vito-bc 04 review; quantpedia.com blocked.

Bui & Nguyen, 'Systematic Trend-Following with Adaptive Portfolio Construction' (arXiv 2602.11708, Feb 2026, not peer-reviewed; long-short Binance futures, 4 bp taker fees, ~134% monthly turnover): vanilla post-cost time-series momentum on 2022-2024 crypto scored Sharpe 0.65 (1-month lookback) / 0.54 (3-month) with max drawdown -34.8%/-38.2%; vol-scaling was required to reach 1.83 and the headline 2.41 Sharpe; its own bear-regime Sharpe is -0.31. Cited by two 2026 practitioner reviews as evidence that unscaled trend is marginal after costs even in a pro-trend paper.

Volatility-scaled entries: Man Group ('Crypto. Too Hot to Handle?', Sep 2012-Dec 2024) reports scaling BTC to a 30% ex-ante vol target adds ~0.4 Sharpe and improves expected shortfall, but turnover and transaction costs are not quantified; the 2026-09-17 review found no crypto source with net-of-cost turnover accounting for vol targeting and classifies it as 'a risk transform, not a return source'. A 2026-06 multi-gate practitioner harness (kimlage/crypto-edge-search) KILLed the Moreira-Muir vol-managed family on crypto: lift flips negative OOS (-0.17), fails a GARCH zero-edge surrogate (p=0.386), PBO=0.95. Grobys et al. (FMPM Dec 2025) find crypto momentum 'is subject to severe crashes' and that vol management mitigates them.

kimlage/crypto-edge-search (audited 2026-06): a systematic hunt over ~30 crypto majors with net-of-cost (taker ~4 bp/side), random-baseline, surrogate, holdout, Deflated-Sharpe and haircut gates ended with '0 clean SURVIVE; 1 weak PROMISING; everything else KILL'. Specific KILLs: day-of-week (~0 after drift removal; tail-driven by shared crash Wednesdays); reversal/Bollinger-%b mean reversion ('these majors trend daily, not revert - wrong-signed in every calendar year'); time-series momentum (all KILL net of crypto cost; 12-month lookback worst; apparent trend return is long-beta to the bull); XS momentum; PCA stat-arb (gross residual-reversion Sharpe negative); microstructure overlays (realistic cost kills all 15m/30m variants). Only perpetual-funding carry and dated-futures basis passed full-sample gates, as sub-risk-free regime trades (thin unlevered ~4.9%/yr excess, t=2.41).

Jaquart, Dann & Weinhardt, 'Short-term Bitcoin market prediction via machine learning', Journal of Finance and Data Science 7:45-66 (2021): BTC directional predictability at 1- to 60-minute horizons with Diebold-Mariano tests; statistically significant prediction only at short horizons (<=15 min), and a very short-horizon trading strategy became negative after realistic transaction costs. Summarised in two independent GitHub research notes (anilmercanoglu-debug/projectA chance-vs-signal.md; shinji-ogasa/UniDream); KIT repository link cited there.

Financial Innovation (2025) 'Algorithmic crypto trading using information-driven bars, triple barrier labeling and deep learning' (10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w; full article text read from a GitHub-hosted fetch): BTC/ETH tick data Jan 2018-Jun 2023, 0.1% Binance fee charged per open and close, 456-day test period in which buy-and-hold lost 34% (BTC) and 44% (ETH). Conventional time-bar sampling with next-bar labeling 'yielded negative results in all experiments' even where hourly BTC direction was predicted with 58.8% accuracy, 'due to transaction costs'; only CUSUM-filtered bars (2% threshold) combined with triple-barrier labels (symmetric 2.5%/5% profit/stop barriers, 24-bar time limit, trades only when P(up)>60% or <40%) were consistently positive after costs. Authors state intervals shorter than 1h 'are unlikely to offset transaction costs' and that most outcomes lean negative even with state-of-the-art deep learning.

Fayyaz, Jabbar, Qureshi & Jalil, 'A Frequency-Controlled Comparison of Tick- and Minute-Based Information Bars for Cryptocurrency Markets' (arXiv 2608.26158, Aug 2026), Binance BTC perp 2020-2025, walk-forward RF/GB/SVM on RSI/Bollinger/MACD features, 2-4 bp taker fees: all information-bar models score near chance (AUC 0.498-0.596); tree models overfit to local mean reversion in a 14x bull market (predicting 'up' only 7% of the time vs 52% positive bars) and produced -99.9% to -100% cumulative returns, still -40.2% with fees set to zero; a 71,619-trade tick-volatility bar configuration showed an 'annualization mirage' Sharpe of 19.75 at 54% accuracy, which the authors flag as a methodological hazard for evaluating high-turnover crypto strategies. Secondhand via HCH725/alpha-strategy-research scout note.

Caporale & Plastun: 'Price overreactions in the cryptocurrency market' (Journal of Economic Studies 46(5), 2019; BTC/LTC/XRP/DASH) concludes 'a strategy based on counter-movements after overreactions is not profitable' and the inertia strategy is 'not statistically different from the random ones'; the companion 'Momentum effects in the cryptocurrency market after one-day abnormal returns' (FMPM 34, 2020; BTC/ETH/LTC hourly 2017-2019) finds next-morning continuation for BTC after negative overreaction days and contrarian behaviour only for ETH. Zaremba et al. (IRFA 2021, >3,600 coins) find daily reversal only in illiquid coins while 'the largest, most tradeable coins exhibit daily momentum, not reversal'. Secondhand via Vito-bc 03-entry-filter-evidence.md.

Grobys, Ahmed & Sapkota, 'Technical trading rules in the cryptocurrency market', Finance Research Letters 32 (2020), 11 most-traded coins daily 2016-2018, long-only variable-MA rules: (1,20) VMA earned 45.63% p.a. vs 36.87% buy-and-hold (+8.76% p.a. excess, jointly significant chi2=33.10, p<0.01); (1,150) and (1,200) rules had no significant payoff for any altcoin ('applying longer time horizons did not generate profits'); cryptos described as 'rather short-memory processes'. Three-year single-cycle sample; transaction-cost treatment not visible in the sections read. Secondhand via keel source-74 and Vito-bc 03 review.

Anghel, Finance Research Letters (2021): after controlling for data snooping and market frictions in cryptocurrency technical trading, 'statistically significant positive excess returns are rarely achieved, independent of the data sampling frequency'; rule performance correlates with beta and idiosyncratic volatility, i.e. rules mostly harvest market risk premia. Secondhand via Vito-bc 02-strategy-families-cost-tolerance.md.

Fieberg, Liedtke, Poddig, Walker & Zaremba, 'A Trend Factor for the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns' (JFQA 60, 2025, open access): CTREND aggregates 28 technical signals via ML across >3,000 coins Apr 2015-May 2022; long-short value-weighted quintile spread 3.87%/week gross with 68%/week turnover, net 2.90%/2.62%/2.35% at one-way costs of 30/40, 40/50, 50/60 bp; break-even one-way cost 1.41% (0.88% at 5% significance), 1.25%/0.70% for the largest 100 coins. It is cross-sectional and requires shorting; whether a single-coin long-only analogue survives costs is untested. This is the highest explicitly modeled cost level found in the peer-reviewed crypto literature.

Han, Kang & Ryu, '...under Realistic Assumptions' (SSRN 4675565, Dec 2023, abstract-level): in crypto 'evidence of time-series momentum is strong, whereas evidence of cross-sectional momentum is weak'; once transaction costs and daily price fluctuations (margin/liquidation) are modeled, 'many momentum portfolios are liquidated and many with statistically significant returns earn insignificant profits'. Relatedly, Ammann et al. (2022, survivorship-free universe) shrink the crypto momentum premium from 2.51%/week in top-100 survivors to 0.13%/week (t=0.13) across all coins.

Intraday seasonality with claimed post-fee profit: Shen, Urquhart & Wang, 'Bitcoin intraday time series momentum', Financial Review 57(2) (2022) report that the first-half-hour return positively predicts the last-half-hour return, with a certainty-equivalent gain of 5.95% p.a. over a random walk and abnormal returns remaining positive after fees (especially for leveraged investors); Miralles-Quiros & Miralles-Quiros (Oeconomia Copernicana 13(3), 2022) use Kraken hourly closes 2016-2021 in a weekday x hour event study and state a strategy built on the significant hours out-Sharpes buy-and-hold. Both are secondhand (the reviewer grades the Shen figures 'D' because the publisher and repository PDFs were blocked), and practitioner notes warn that 7 days x 24 hours x many coins is a severe multiple-testing space.

Pricetab 'TODAY' research log (Coinbase daily data 2015-2026, 8 coins x 8 rules, costed): 'Every rule cuts the fall; almost none pays for it' - rules reduced worst drawdown vs holding in 59 of 64 rule x coin pairs but beat holding on return in only 28 of 64 (a coin flip); 'Above SMA 200' median +65% return, Sharpe 0.47, max DD 81%, beat holding on 4 of 8 coins; 'SMA 50/200 cross' median +119%, Sharpe 0.53, DD 76%, beat holding 3 of 8 and fell from rank 4 (2015-2021) to rank 8 (2021-2026); raising the assumed round-trip fee cut MACD's median return from +1006% to +343%; zero rules survived Holm-Bonferroni.

Alorse/pinescript-strategies automated PineTS backtests of 17 public TradingView strategies (trend, momentum, mean-reversion, grid) on BTCUSDT daily bars, generated 2026-08-25: on the 2025-01-01 to 2026-08-25 snapshot (602 bars) every strategy with trades had a NEGATIVE Sharpe (-0.05 to -1.73), and on 2022-2024 (731 bars) the best Sharpe was 0.175 with net +8.75%; the Bollinger-based mean-reversion strategies scored -7.2% (2022-24) and -1.9% (2025-26). Author caveats: single symbol, approximate commission rounding, comparison baseline only.

Scalping arithmetic from a 2026 practitioner note (viceenterprises2022-design, Hyperliquid 1.5 bp maker / 4.5 bp taker): with a 9 bp taker round trip, 5-minute BTC scalping must capture 58% of a one-sigma move (15.4 bp) just to break even, 15-minute 34%, 1-hour 17%, 4-hour 8%; 'No published intraday effect is that large. This horizon is not reachable with taker execution', and academic intraday effects 'typically report 1-5 bps... economically dead once you subtract 9 bps of fees'. At Coinbase retail tiers the round trip is roughly 10-20x larger. A separate log (infornet1/trading) reports a long-only RSI-oversold dip-buy on 15m BTC in 2024-2025 with a 22.9% win rate over 175 trades.

Backtest-overfitting caveats to apply to any flip-strategy comparison: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu (Notices of the AMS, 2014) show that trying N=10 configurations of strategies whose true Sharpe is zero yields an expected best-of-sweep Sharpe of 1.57 (2.6 at N=128), that a hold-out split 'does not take into account the number of trials attempted', and give a minimum backtest length formula; McLean & Pontiff document anomaly returns averaging -26% out-of-sample and -58% post-publication. Freqtrade's official docs warn that 'Many strategies, without the programmer knowing, have fallen prey to lookahead bias', that backtests fill at requested price with no slippage, and that 'backtesting will never replace running a strategy in dry-run mode'.

Regime caveats: BTC break-even and profitability results cluster in samples ending 2017-2019 (Gerritsen, Hudson & Urquhart, Detzel, Grobys) when the market was measurably less efficient; Hudson & Urquhart's own H1 2018 out-of-sample BTC test was negative; Bysik & Slepaczuk's 2018-2026 folds show fold-level instability; the 2026-09-17 review lists a '2026 whipsaw (BTC -32.9% H1 then +25% Aug)' and notes that in 2025 the average reporting crypto fund returned -7.2% (median -5.2%, only 37% of 84 funds positive), with 409 closed funds dropped from the index. The review's summary: documented decay is clearest for mean reversion, size, calendar anomalies and parameter-optimised MA rules, while direct evidence that trend/breakout decayed after 2021 is thin.

open_questions: No peer-reviewed or preprint study was found that explicitly backtests fixed 1.5% / 2% / 3-5% take-profit 'flip' strategies on spot BTC at retail fee tiers (0.5-1.2% per side); the closest evidence (optional-stopping argument, Acar & Toffel on equities/bonds, one 2020-2025 hobbyist backtest) is indirect. The user's paper-trading harness will have to generate this comparison itself.

The reported Coinbase Advanced fee change to 0.50% maker / 0.90% taker on 2026-09-16 could not be verified on Coinbase's own site (blocked); Kraken Pro's current fee schedule was not found at all in this sweep. Fee tier is the single most decision-relevant number and must be confirmed from the user's own account before any simulation.

Primary texts for most papers (arXiv, SSRN, ScienceDirect, Springer, Wiley, BIS, MDPI) were unreachable; only Gerritsen 2020, Hudson & Urquhart 2021 and the 2025 Financial Innovation triple-barrier paper were read in (mirrored) full text. Figures for Detzel 2021, Bysik & Slepaczuk 2026, Kitron & Wengrowicz 2026, Chen et al. 2025 (grid), Zarattini 2025, Shen et al. 2022 and Kang & Ryu 2026 are secondhand extractions and should be spot-checked against the originals when the user's own machine has open web access.

Whether the 15-minute mean-reversion edge (arXiv 2608.21888) is capturable with maker (post-only) limit orders at Coinbase/Kraken retail maker fees was not established; the paper's own conclusion is 'no' at benchmark spot costs, but maker fill rates and adverse selection for a small account were not studied.

Time-of-day effects: no source with verifiable post-fee magnitudes on 2024-2026 data was found; the Shen et al. 2022 (first half-hour predicts last half-hour) and Miralles-Quiros 2022 (weekday x hour) claims of beating buy-and-hold after fees remain unverified and carry a large multiple-testing burden.

Grid trading: no direct peer-reviewed crypto grid study reports drawdown relative to holding; the dynamic-grid preprint (arXiv 2506.11921) does not state fee assumptions in its abstract and its enhanced variant retains beta. Whether any grid spacing clears 2x a 1-1.8% round trip on BTC with acceptable time-in-range is untested.

Volatility-scaled entries / vol targeting: no crypto source reports net-of-cost turnover accounting for a single-asset vol-target overlay; the +0.4 Sharpe figure (Man Group) is gross and portfolio-level.

200-day moving average specifically: Detzel et al. tested lookbacks only up to 100 days; the 200-day regime filter evidence found is practitioner-grade (Pricetab: median Sharpe 0.47, beats holding on return in 4 of 8 coins; yongkang: golden cross 44% CAGR / -57% DD vs HODL 63% / -77%, 2020-2025 only). A clean 2018-2026 BTC test of 200-DMA vs 12-week trend vs buy-and-hold at the user's fee tier is not available.

The claimed 2026 market regime (BTC -32.9% in H1 2026 then +25% in Aug 2026, average crypto fund -7.2% in 2025) comes from one secondhand review and was not independently confirmed because market-data and news domains are blocked.

Zarattini, Pagani & Barbon 2025 (Donchian ensemble, Sharpe 1.58 net of 0.1-0.5% fees) is the most encouraging trend result but its fee-sensitivity table, turnover and 2022 sub-period were not verifiable; it is a 20-coin rotational portfolio, not a BTC-only strategy.

research:target-math.summary:
TARGET-MATH SWEEP (2026-09-19). Method note: WebSearch was unavailable (session budget 200/200 exhausted before this sweep) and the proxy blocks Wikipedia/arXiv/SSRN/FRED/exchange APIs/bot vendors, so evidence comes from ~20 GitHub searches, raw-GitHub fetches, and direct computation on ff137/bitstamp-btcusd-minute-data (Bitstamp BTC/USD 1-min OHLC, gap-free, 2012-01-01 to 2026-09-19 01:41 UTC). Scripts and CSV outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crushpaper/726f4765-ef02-5a68-a568-426e246fec70/scratchpad (barrier_study.py, barrier_full.csv, barrier_2026.csv).

(1) REALIZED VOL. BTC daily close-to-close vol was 41.9% annualized in 2025 (daily sd 2.20%, mean |move| 1.57%) and 46.5% in 2026 YTD (daily sd 2.43%); last 30d 44.3%, last 90d 38.0% (vs 80-93% in 2017-2021). Hourly sd is ~0.47% (2025: 0.478%, 2026: 0.466%); a 1h move >1% happens ~4.5% of hours, >2% ~0.7%. Vol is concentrated 13-17 UTC (hourly sd 0.61-0.72%) vs 0.34-0.37% in the 04-05/10-11 UTC lulls; Saturdays 0.28% vs Mondays 0.56%. Daily high-low range: median 2.94% of open; the day's range reaches 2% on 73% of days, 3% on 48%, 5% on 16%. Price fell -16.3% over the study window (96,946 to 81,102). External 2026 datapoints corroborate a 35-55% band with spikes (RV7 71.5% on 2026-06-08; DVOL 43.1% vs RV7 35.2% for week ending 2026-04-10; HV30 54.3% on 2026-03-12).

(2) DOUBLE-BARRIER MATH. Driftless: P(hit +a before -b) = b/(a+b); expected time = a*b/sigma^2 (gambler's-ruin duration a(N-a)). At 44% annualized vol, symmetric brackets give expected hit times of 10h (1.5%), 18h (2%), 41h (3%), 113h (5%); 2%TP/4%SL wins 67% with 37h; 2%TP/10%SL wins 84% with 94h. Empirically (14,159 top-of-hour entries, 2025-01-07 to 2026-08-19, 30-day cap, fills at minute high/low): symmetric 1.5%/2%/3%/5% brackets resolved in favour of the target 50.3%/48.8%/49.1%/50.5% of the time with medians 12h/20h/42h/112h and means 19h/31h/64h/148h (means run ~1.7-2x the Brownian formula because of vol clustering; medians match it). 2%/4% won 64.4% (theory 67.3%); 2%/10% won 81.2%; 2% target with no stop 'won' 84.3% but 15.7% of trades were still open after 30 days. In 2026 YTD the symmetric 2% and 3% brackets won only 46.6%/46.2% because of negative drift.

(3) WHY HIGH WIN RATE CAN STILL LOSE. Optional stopping theorem: a stop/target bracket cannot change expectancy on a martingale, it only trades hit-rate for payoff size (Acar & Toffel: 'stop-loss and take-profit strategies are a cost for doing business'; Kaminski & Lo: under the random walk simple stops always reduce expected return). Break-even win rate = (SL + round-trip fee)/(TP + SL), so the extra edge needed over the coin-flip base is fee/(TP+SL): at 2%/2% that is +8 pts (Kraken maker 0.32% RT), +13 (Kraken taker 0.52%), +20 (Coinbase Advanced maker 0.8%), +30 (Coinbase Advanced taker 1.2%). Empirically the 2%/2% bracket had gross expectancy -0.05%/trade and 23.6 trades/month, i.e. roughly -9% to -29% per month net depending on fee tier; 2%TP/10%SL had 81% wins, -0.12% gross, and ~-8%/month at Coinbase taker fees. Only 5% brackets showed slightly positive gross expectancy (+0.14 to +0.23%/trade), which fees at 0.32-1.2% RT erase. Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, Aug 2026, 183 Binance pairs, holdout to 2026-08-08) find the strongest short-horizon reversal edge is ~1.3 bp/trade vs 5 bp maker / 10-20 bp taker costs. Hudson & Urquhart: break-even one-way cost for BTC technical rules tops out at 57.5-66.4 bp, far below the user's 60-120 bp round trip; no peer-reviewed study tests >=1.5% round-trip costs.

(4) GRID/FLIP BOT DATA. Chen, Chen & Jang (arXiv 2506.11921): a static grid has zero expected profit before fees under a symmetric random walk; their dynamic grid beat buy-and-hold on BTC/ETH (Jan 2021-Jul 2024) 'largely due to the significant rise in cryptocurrency prices'. Nguyen & Bui (SSRN 6280958): delta-neutral grid market-making, Gate.io BTCUSDT Nov-Dec 2025, 52 days: +37%, Sharpe >3, MDD <8%, with 76% of P&L from spread and 6% from maker rebate; the unit economics of a 0.10% cycle flip from +0.15% with a -0.025% rebate to -0.10% at a 0.10% retail maker fee. A practitioner's Pionex BTC/USDT grid returned ~4.8% over 90 days in a flat Jan-Apr 2026 period; a grid running 200 trades/month at 0.05%/trade pays ~10%/yr in fees. No audited platform statistics were found.

For a fair (driftless) random walk the probability of reaching the upper barrier before the lower one is the starting fraction of the distance, P = a/(a+b) toward the target b away (gambler's ruin P_i = i/N), and the expected number of unit steps to absorption is D_i = i(N-i), i.e. a*b; in continuous time this is E[T] = a*b/sigma^2. Both results follow from optional stopping applied to the martingales S_n and S_n^2 - n.

Under a Brownian-motion model at 44% annualized vol (hourly sigma 0.470%), the expected time to hit either side of a symmetric bracket is 10.2 h at 1.5%, 18.1 h at 2%, 40.7 h (1.7 d) at 3% and 113 h (4.7 d) at 5%; a 2% target with a 4% stop wins 67.3% of the time with expected duration 36.6 h, and a 2% target with a 10% stop wins 84.2% with expected duration 94 h. Gross expectancy before fees is ~0 in every case. (Computed from the formulas in the cited lesson.)

Empirical double-barrier test on 14,159 top-of-hour entries (2025-01-07 to 2026-08-19, fills at minute high/low, 30-day cap): symmetric 1.5%/2%/3%/5% brackets hit the target first 50.3%/48.8%/49.1%/50.5% of the time; median time to resolution was 12.2 h/20.4 h/42.1 h/111.7 h, mean 19.4 h/30.5 h/63.6 h/148 h, and 90th percentile 46 h/69 h/146 h/332 h. Means are ~1.7-2x the Brownian formula (9.8/17.4/39/109 h) because of vol clustering, while medians roughly match it.

Asymmetric brackets behave as theory predicts: over 2025-01-07 to 2026-08-19 a 2% target with a 4% stop won 64.4% (theory 67.3%), a 2% target with a 10% stop won 81.2% (theory 84.2%) but had gross expectancy -0.12%/trade and mean hold 111 h, and a 2% target with no stop 'won' 84.3% of trades yet 15.7% were still open after 30 days with gross expectancy -0.59%/trade; a 1.5% target with a 10% stop won 85.1% with gross expectancy -0.13%.

In the 2026-01-01 to 2026-08-19 sub-window (5,544 entries) the symmetric 2% and 3% brackets hit the target first only 46.6% and 46.2% of the time (gross expectancy -0.14% and -0.23% per trade before any fees) because BTC drifted down; drift, not bracket geometry, dominates flip P&L over months. Only the 5% brackets showed positive gross expectancy (+0.44%/trade symmetric, +0.34% with 10% stop) at 2.8-4.3 trades/month.

The optional stopping theorem states E[X_tau] = E[X_0] for a martingale under bounded stopping time, bounded increments with finite E[tau], or uniform integrability; applied to gambler's ruin it yields P(reach N) = a/N. Consequently a take-profit/stop-loss bracket, which is a stopping rule, cannot create positive expectation on a fair game - it only moves probability mass between hit rate and payoff size.

Acar & Toffel (Institute of Actuaries, 2000) conclude verbatim that 'under the random walk assumption, stop-loss and take profits strategies are a cost for doing business. Such rules cannot beat buy and hold'; their S&P 500 1.10% take-profit realized 6.30%/yr vs 8.95% expected, and Kaminski & Lo (J. Financial Markets 2014) show that under the random walk hypothesis simple stop-loss rules always decrease expected return (their positive result is for monthly futures 1950-2004, not intraday crypto).

Break-even win rate for a bracket is P* = (SL + fee_RT)/(TP + SL), while the driftless base rate is ~SL/(TP+SL), so the edge required over a coin flip is fee_RT/(TP+SL). At a 2%/2% bracket the required win rate is 58% at 0.32% round trip (Kraken maker 0.16% x2), 63% at 0.52% (Kraken taker), 70% at 0.80% (Coinbase Advanced maker 0.4% x2) and 80% at 1.20% (Coinbase Advanced taker 0.6% x2); at 1.5%/1.5% it is 61%/67%/77%/90%.

ccxt's exchange descriptors list Kraken spot fees at 0.26% taker / 0.16% maker for 30-day volume under $50k (falling to 0.10%/0.00% above $10M) and Coinbase Advanced Trade at 0.6% taker / 0.4% maker in the lowest tier (0.4%/0.25% from $10k, 0.25%/0.15% from $50k), with the file's default set to 1.2%/0.6% citing an 'Advanced 1' $0-$1,000 pricing tier - verify the live schedule before relying on these.

Empirical net expectancy per trade for the 2%/2% bracket over 2025-01-07 to 2026-08-19 was -0.05% gross and -0.37%/-0.57%/-0.85%/-1.25% after 0.32%/0.52%/0.80%/1.20% round-trip fees; at the observed 23.6 trades/month with immediate re-entry that is roughly -9% to -29% of the flip pool per month. The 1.5%/1.5% bracket (37 trades/month) is worse; only the 5% brackets stay near break-even and only at Kraken-maker-level fees.

Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, 22 Aug 2026; 183 Binance USDT pairs on 15-minute bars, in-sample 2025-01-01 to 2026-02-08, frozen holdout 2026-02-12 to 2026-08-08) find a persistent short-horizon reversal whose gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp per trade, against roughly 5 bp round-trip at maker fees and 10-20 bp at taker fees - i.e. the best-measured short-horizon edge is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than retail spot costs.

Hudson & Urquhart (Annals of OR 2021, ~15,000 technical rules on BTC/ETH/XRP/LTC to end-2017) report break-even one-way costs for Bitcoin rules topping out at 66.41 bp (CoinDesk) and 57.51 bp (Bitstamp), and their pure out-of-sample H1-2018 test gave negative annualized results; a 2026-09-17 literature map concludes 'no study tests a >=1.5% round-trip cost on spot' and that literature cost assumptions cluster at 4-60 bp.

A 2026 range-bar research note documents the failure mode directly: a very tight take-profit 'will trigger constantly on Gaussian noise alone, creating an artificially inflated win rate' while 'the extremely wide stop loss survives simply because the random walk has not yet drifted far enough to hit it' - a 5:1 adverse risk/reward profile the author calls 'picking up pennies in front of a steamroller', which Kelly sizing on the raw win rate actively rewards.

A systematic setup-timing study (2R fixed target, 10% capped risk) found hit rate and expectancy 'come apart': hit rate rose monotonically across signal quintiles while the best-hit-rate bucket had the worst expectancy of the five, and no conditioner tested sorted expectancy at all - only hit rate.

Chen, Chen & Jang (arXiv 2506.11921, 2025) prove analytically that under a symmetric random walk with fees ignored a classical static grid has zero expected profit; their Dynamic Grid Trading beat buy-and-hold on BTC and ETH over Jan 2021-Jul 2024 with lower drawdown, but the authors state this 'is largely due to the significant rise in cryptocurrency prices', i.e. retained beta rather than market-neutral alpha.

Nguyen & Bui (SSRN 6280958, 2026) report a delta-neutral grid market-maker on Gate.io BTCUSDT over 52 trading days in Nov-Dec 2025 returning ~37% with daily Sharpe >3 and MDD <8%, with ~76% of P&L from spread/grid, ~18% funding and ~6% maker rebate; the reviewing note shows the 0.10%-spread cycle is +0.15% with a -0.025% rebate but -0.05% at a 0.075% fee and -0.10% at a 0.10% retail maker fee, and flags an unresolved capital-sizing inconsistency and an optimistic fill model (~14,000 assumed fills).

This is vendor-published, covers a strong bull period, and no fees or later periods are stated.

A practitioner blog (April 2026) reports a Pionex BTC/USDT grid bot set up in January 2026 returned about 4.8% over 90 days during a flat period, notes Pionex charges 0.05% per trade, and warns that running 200 trades/month costs about 10% annualized in fees on active capital; it characterizes the '12-25% annualized' claims of AI-bot platforms as top-quartile performance under favorable conditions, not a baseline.

Neither is audited.

A March 2026 strategy review of a live retail system running 1.5-3% take-profits with 1-2% stops on hourly bars reported a 34% win rate across 856 trades and +0.9% ROI, computing expectancy of 0.34 x 2.25% - 0.66 x 1.5% = -0.225% per trade; it also relays a practitioner finding that grid bots 'can pull in ~1% a day on paper, but once you subtract exchange fees, slippage, and funding costs, about 0.8% of that disappears'.

Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (arXiv 2410.15195, rev. 2025-08-01; Deribit options 2017-2022, 27-day horizon) estimate BTC's annualized variance risk premium at 0.14 overall, with physical variance 0.29 (~54% vol) in the low-vol regime and 0.74 (~86% vol) in the high-vol regime, and find the premium is higher in the low-vol regime - context for why implied vol usually sits above realized in calm periods.

A BTC/USDT 1-hour volatility-forecasting project (65k Binance bars 2019-2026) estimates a GJR-GARCH(1,1) with persistence 0.977 and ~30-hour half-life and near-zero leverage effect at 1h, and reports that 'even moments (variance, RV) generalize out-of-sample on this asset, odd moments (sign, skew) do not' - its variance forecast beats HAR baselines by ~32% QLIKE while its directional and short-vol arms failed pre-registered gates.
